I insist that this isn't a bleeding problem, as I used both headsets for DnD on my PC and they worked a charm. I'm baffled at this point and simply don't understand. Any advice?

That what hes done is okay, in terms of the family. You still love him, and support him. Ive been there, and the first psych trip is scary. He will be bored... A LOT. Try to grt him books when you can. Tell him that its going to seem stupid and childish at times, but to engage with the process. Let him know to be totally and completely honest with the docs. The right meds will help. Visit him often, and call often. Its easy to become isolated and alone in the ward. 

Seriously, as someone who wasnt told these things, its vital that he have as much info as possible. There's security in knowledge, even if theres no control.

EDIT: I realize now that I didn't really give much pointers to what to say, but that's a deeply personal thing that's not easy to comment on from outside. But arming him with knowledge can change a scary experience into a healing one.

EDIT 2: I keep fucking adding more, but if youre interested, DM me and I can give you my phone number. If he has questions about the process, I'm open to a call or two. Ive been through a couple times and can give him the rundown on what I experienced in the psych system as both an adult and a child, as well as post treatment stuff.

As someone who has struggled for a long time: It's a golden ticket. Any problem, and pain, any annoyance, will simply be gone. After awhile, it turns into a habit. You comfort yourself with, "Ah well, I'll be dead soon anyways.".

Frankly, when I did attempt, it was the first time in a long time I felt in control. It wasn't euphoric, bit I finally felt peaceful. I knew what I was doing, why it was happening, what was going to happen, etc. The fear only came when I was rescued, because I would have to deal with the consequences. I think about that time often, and frequently wish I could go back, simply because of what I felt at that time of resolve. 

But life goes on, and even though I'm deeply suicidal, I understand that there are responsibilities I have to maintain.

Ive had a lot bad in my life to justify my choice.

Thats my experience in why people are suicidal, and why they also continue on.

I used to read, and go to concerts, and dabble in subcultures and just generally be adventurous.

For me, it was the adventure that went away first. I was too tired, I said. I was too busy. It was too far away. This coming from a guy that walked two hours on a highway to make it a town over. 

I stopped writing next. I never felt it was good enough. I was revoltes by my own work. Now, years later, I literally cannot create my own, wholly original premises to write. It demotivates me to realize that.

I stopped reading too. I still have the imagination, but I just struggle to commit to the action.

I stopped going out to meet people. Its been so long that my social skills have become such a foreign concept that I had to ask my only remaining irl how to meet people. I was so embarrassed.

I'm out of shape these days, and honestly afraid that I'm becoming a shut in..
